title: Cross-layer scale redistribution harness for activation-aware INT8 quant and runtime kernel fallbacks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: implement a cross-layer scale redistribution (CLS) calibration and validation harness that produces stable activation-aware INT8 profiles (SmoothQuant-like redistribution) and a lightweight runtime kernel adapter with deterministic fallback paths. This ticket covers: 1) a calibration pipeline that computes layer-pair scaling factors and per-channel quant parameters; 2) an accuracy-validation suite against held-out eval prompts/tasks to detect quality regressions; 3) runtime kernel shims that apply redistributions at inference time or fall back to per-layer FP16 execution when accuracy or perf constraints are violated. Motivation: some transformer layers have imbalanced activation distributions that break uniform INT8 quantization. Redistributing scales across attention and MLP pairs reduces quantization error without model retraining. We need an engineering-first pipeline that integrates with our CI/CD, produces reproducible profiles, and exposes runtime hooks for canaryed rollout on Dedicated and Hosted environments.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces reproducible .quant.json profiles for 4 reference models (gpt-medium, llama-2-7b, mpt-7b-instruct, and a KV-cache heavy chat model) with documented seed and dataset used

End-to-end accuracy delta for representative eval suites is within configured guardrails (<= 1.5% relative for perplexity-based benchmarks, <= 0.8% for task-specific metrics) compared to FP16 baseline
Runtime kernel adapter supports: (a) in-place layer-pair scale application, (b) fallback to per-layer FP16 for failing layers, (c) switchable via model manifest and runtime flag
Automated CI checks that validate produced quant profiles against a small smoke eval and reject candidate profiles that fail accuracy or memory regression thresholds
Perf regression under nightly CI < 10% token/sec compared to previous INT8 baseline for the same hardware and batch sizes, and memory footprint < 95% of FP16 in end-to-end runs
Design doc and benchmark artifacts (plots, per-layer error tables) published and linked in the ticket

calibration_workflow: We will adopt a two-stage calibration: 1) data collection pass with representative inputs (mix of short/long contexts, chat-like multi-turn traces, instruction-style prompts) seeded for reproducibility; 2) optimization pass that computes cross-layer scale factors for attention->mlp pairs using a constrained least-squares objective that minimizes activation quantization error under per-channel quantization constraints. Default sample budget is 5k tokens per model for an initial profile (can be increased for high-sensitivity customers). Profiles include per-tensor scale, zero-point (if used), and a small metadata block with seed, hardware tag, and calibration dataset hash. We will track calibration metrics (L2 error, KL between FP16 and dequantized INT8 activations, and end-task metric delta) and store artifacts in an S3 bucket with immutable versioning.
runtime_changes: Add a minimal kernel shim that, at model load, reads the .quant.json and computes per-layer multiplicative factors applied to the weight or activation pathways. Adapter requirements: deterministic numerics across hosts, low overhead (<2% latency increase), support for streaming/kv-cache where applicable. Fallback policy: if a layer's validation score (computed during CI or live shadow eval) exceeds a threshold, mark layer as 'no-redistribute' and execute FP16 path for that layer only. For Dedicated capacity, expose a routing policy to prefer 'redistribute-enabled' nodes for customers who opt in. For Hosted, default to gradual canary: 1%->10%->50%->100% rollout tied to monitored QA metrics.
perf_targets: Target median generation latency regressions < 5% across batch sizes 1..8 on A100 and RTX6000. Token throughput delta vs current INT8 baseline must be >= 0% (ideally positive). Memory savings goal: 30-45% reduction vs FP16 for models tested. Kernel overhead budget: adapter path < 2 microseconds per token for fused matmul kernels.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal spike and offline validation (this ticket)
Phase 1: Canary on Dedicated test cluster with synthetic traffic (10 nodes)
Phase 2: Small customer opt-in via feature flag (2 customers)
Phase 3: Gradual hosted rollout with canary gates and rollback automation
Phase 4: Promote profiles to default for compatible model variants after 4 weeks of stable metrics
ci_validation: Unit tests for redistribution math and profile parser
Integration test: apply profile to a micro model and compare activations against FP16 seed within thresholds
Nightly smoke: run 200 prompt evals across reference models and assert task-metric deltas and latency constraints
Golden profiles: store canonical profiles and reject CI artifacts that drift beyond tolerances without documented cause
notes: Spike results (2025-02-20): CLS reduced layerwise KL by median 3.2x on gpt-medium with 1k sample calibration; pay attention to attention->mlp pair ordering in fused architectures.
Design decision 2025-02-25: prefer multiplicative redistribution applied to weights over activation rescaling at runtime for lower numerical jitter across compilers.
Open risk: per-channel quantization interacts with kernel-level vectorization; need kernel team signoff before merging fused implementation.
Customer ask: compliance-sensitive workloads require audit logging of applied redistributions — add metadata and HMAC signing for profiles.
